Shift every Latin letter of a text a number of places along the alphabet, keeping its case and everything else.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/rotational-cipher) (MIT). Listed under [Encoding & Ciphers](/examples/?subject=encoding-and-ciphers).

```nomi-run
// FILE: rotational_cipher.nomi
//# The rotational (Caesar) cipher over the Latin alphabet.

/// `text` with every Latin letter moved `key` places along the alphabet,
/// wrapping from `z` to `a` and keeping its case. Everything else is kept.
pub fn rotate(text: String, key: Int) -> String {
    cipher = Map.merge(shifted('a'..='z', key), shifted('A'..='Z', key))

    text
    |> String.to_codepoints()
    |> Iter.map(fn letter -> Map.get(cipher, letter) |> Maybe.with_default(letter))
    |> Iter.to_list()
    |> String.from_codepoints()
}

/// Maps each letter of `alphabet` to the letter `key` places after it.
fn shifted(alphabet: Range<Codepoint>, key: Int) -> Map<Codepoint, Codepoint> {
    rotated = alphabet |> Iter.cycle() |> Iter.drop(Int.modulo(key, 26))
    Iter.zip(alphabet, rotated) |> Iter.to_map()
}

// FILE: rotational_cipher_test.nomi
import rotational_cipher

test "rotate" {
    cases = [
        #("rotate a by 0, same output as input", "a", 0, "a"),
        #("rotate a by 1", "a", 1, "b"),
        #("rotate a by 26, same output as input", "a", 26, "a"),
        #("rotate m by 13", "m", 13, "z"),
        #("rotate n by 13 with wrap around alphabet", "n", 13, "a"),
        #("rotate capital letters", "OMG", 5, "TRL"),
        #("rotate spaces", "O M G", 5, "T R L"),
        #("rotate numbers", "Testing 1 2 3 testing", 4, "Xiwxmrk 1 2 3 xiwxmrk"),
        #("rotate punctuation", "Let's eat, Grandma!", 21, "Gzo'n zvo, Bmviyhv!"),
        #(
            "rotate all letters",
            "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
            13,
            "Gur dhvpx oebja sbk whzcf bire gur ynml qbt.",
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, text, key, expected), description {
        assert rotational_cipher.rotate(text, key) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- The cipher is a `Map<Codepoint, Codepoint>` built once per call from the ranges `'a'..='z'` and `'A'..='Z'`: each range zipped with itself cycled and dropped by the key. A character that is not a key, such as a space or a digit, maps to itself through `Maybe.with_default`.
- The map avoids codepoint arithmetic, which would pick `'a'` or `'A'` by the letter's case, take its offset modulo 26 and turn the sum back with `Int.to_codepoint(...)!`. The map needs none of that, and a character outside both alphabets needs no test of its own.
- `Int.modulo(key, 26)` keeps the key in one turn of the alphabet, so a negative key would rotate backwards. The canonical keys are all from 0 to 26.
- The text is read with `String.to_codepoints`, since the alphabet ranges are codepoints, and written back with `String.from_codepoints`. That takes a `List`, as `to_codepoints` gives one, so the lazy map ends in `Iter.to_list()`.
